original_question: Universal algorithms for multivariate integration are currently known in the paper only for the cube [0,1]^d. Do there exist universal algorithms of the same kind for integration over domains other than [0,1]^d?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Open Problem (p. 114): "So far only the domain [0,1]^d was studied for the construction of universal algorithms. One might speculate that universal algorithms also exist for other domains." This is sharpened in Section 6, A Final Open Problem / Eq. (17) (p. 126), which asks for universal randomized linear algorithms over an open domain D_d ⊂ R^d, ideally with the same optimal error bounds as Theorem 3, known only for ρ = 1 on D_d = [0,1]^d.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right topic: the paper's open problem about extending the universal-integration algorithms beyond the cube [0,1]^d. It also correctly reflects the paper's state-of-the-art claim that the universal constructions discussed there are known only on [0,1]^d, and it asks the intended existence question rather than drifting into a different issue such as tractability or lower bounds.
missing_details: The draft does not specify what 'universal' means in this paper: one and the same randomized algorithm should work across a whole scale of smoothness classes, rather than being retuned to each smoothness parameter k.
It omits the algorithm class used in the paper: randomized linear cubature rules of the form A_n^ω(f) = Σ_{j=1}^n a_j(ω) f(x_j(ω)).
It omits that Section 3 seeks algorithms that are good simultaneously in the randomized worst-case setting and in the deterministic worst-case setting.

It does not name the benchmark results from Theorem 3 that define the target meaning of 'same kind': for isotropic Sobolev smoothness H_d^k with k > d/2, e^ran(A_n,H_d^k) ≍ n^(-k/d-1/2) and e(A_n,H_d^k) ≍ n^(-k/d); for dominating mixed smoothness H_d^{k,mix} with k ∈ N, e^ran(A_n,H_d^{k,mix}) ≍ n^(-k-1/2) and e(A_n,H_d^{k,mix}) ≍ n^(-k)(log n)^((d-1)/2).
It omits that the randomized Frolov algorithm in Theorem 3 is unbiased: E(A_n(f)) = S_d(f).

It does not specify the integration functional. In the nearest Section 3 formulation this is the unweighted integral over [0,1]^d; in the later final open problem it is the weighted functional S(f) = ∫_{D_d} f(x)ρ(x) dx. Since your draft targets the Section 3 open problem, the faithful rewrite should stay with the unweighted case rather than broadening to arbitrary weights.

It does not state the ambient domain assumptions needed to make the question stand-alone. Section 1 normalizes domains by λ_d(D_d) = 1, and Section 4 explains that for non-Lipschitz domains the definitions of Sobolev-type spaces may differ; bounded Lipschitz domains are the clean paper-faithful setting if one wants precise Sobolev notation on general domains.
It omits the paper's suggestion that one might even hope for such algorithms with iid uniformly distributed sample points x_j, which appears in the final open problem.
It does not indicate that the paper allows a weaker fallback target if exact optimality is too much to ask: matching the Theorem 3 rates up to additional logarithmic factors.
refined_question: Let D_d ⊂ R^d be a bounded Lipschitz domain with λ_d(D_d) = 1, and let S_D(f) = ∫_{D_d} f(x) dx. Does there exist, for domains D_d other than [0,1]^d, a universal randomized linear cubature algorithm A_n^ω(f) = Σ_{j=1}^n a_j(ω) f(x_j(ω))—ideally unbiased and possibly with x_j iid uniformly distributed on D_d—such that the same algorithm, without being retuned to the smoothness parameter k, achieves on the corresponding Sobolev scales the cube-optimal orders from Theorem 3 simultaneously in the randomized and deterministic worst-case settings; namely, for all k > d/2 on isotropic Sobolev spaces H^k(D_d), e^ran(A_n,H^k(D_d)) ≍ n^(-k/d-1/2) and e(A_n,H^k(D_d)) ≍ n^(-k/d), and for all k ∈ N on mixed-smoothness spaces H^{k,mix}(D_d), e^ran(A_n,H^{k,mix}(D_d)) ≍ n^(-k-1/2) and e(A_n,H^{k,mix}(D_d)) ≍ n^(-k)(log n)^((d-1)/2); or, if exact optimality is impossible, at least these rates up to additional logarithmic factors?
justification: The exact official formulation closest to your draft is the Section 3 open problem about extending universal algorithms from [0,1]^d to other domains. To make that question stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must import the paper's meaning of universality from Theorem 3: a single randomized linear algorithm, not depending on k, that is simultaneously optimal in randomized and deterministic worst-case error on the Sobolev scales treated there. Section 6 confirms that this is indeed the intended unresolved direction, restating it as a final open problem for general domains and emphasizing that such algorithms are only known for ρ = 1 on [0,1]^d. Section 4 adds the hidden domain caveat: on arbitrary non-Lipschitz domains the relevant Sobolev-space definitions are not canonical, so bounded Lipschitz domains are the cleanest sharp formulation if one wants a fully explicit stand-alone question.
